content.value_statement: Writing Obsidian Desmos blocks is error-prone because settings, equations, points, and restrictions use different syntax. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to produce valid graph blocks with styling, labels, bounds, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Creates Obsidian desmos-graph blocks for functions, points, inequalities, polar equations, and parametric curves.
Chooses correct syntax for settings, equations, point coordinates, and restrictions.
Adds supported colors, line styles, point styles, labels, hidden functions, and graph bounds.
Explains common parser errors and gives corrected graph syntax.
Converts unsupported polar examples into parametric curve forms when needed.
limitations: The skill does not render graphs inside the AI chat.
It does not install or configure the Obsidian plugin.
It cannot confirm plugin version differences unless the user provides them.
It focuses on graph block syntax, not broader calculus instruction.

use_cases.title: Prepare Lesson Graphs
use_cases.description: Create lesson notes with clear Desmos graphs for functions, transformations, and labeled points.

use_cases.title: Study Function Behavior
use_cases.description: Turn homework concepts into Obsidian graphs that compare curves and highlight important coordinates.

use_cases.title: Document Technical Math
use_cases.description: Document equations with consistent graph blocks and concise troubleshooting notes.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Function Graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an Obsidian desmos-graph block for a quadratic and sine curve. Use simple bounds, readable colors, and short labels.

prompt_templates.title: Add Styling and Labels
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a graph with labeled intercepts, two styled curves, and a custom viewport. Avoid unsupported color names.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Parametric Curve
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a parametric curve with control points and helper lines. Use syntax that avoids piecewise parsing errors.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot a Complex Graph
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my graph request for parser problems before writing the block. Explain syntax choices for settings, equations, points, and restrictions.

output_examples.input: Plot sine and cosine over one full period with different line styles.
output_examples.output: A graph block plan with radians mode, balanced bounds, colored curves, and a dashed cosine line.

output_examples.input: Show a circle with the origin and one labeled point on the circumference.
output_examples.output: A graph block plan with a circle equation, labeled points, fixed bounds, and supported colors.

output_examples.input: Fix a graph that uses plain pi in point coordinates.
output_examples.output: A corrected graph explanation that uses Desmos syntax for point coordinates and mathjs syntax for settings.

best_practices: Set viewport bounds before equations when the graph needs a specific range.
Use LaTeX syntax for equations and point coordinates.
Use numeric constants in restrictions because that parser is not LaTeX.
anti_patterns: Mixing mathjs pi syntax into equations or point coordinates.
Using unsupported color names such as gray instead of hex colors.
Putting pipe characters inside labels or absolute value expressions.

faq.question: Does this skill create Obsidian Desmos blocks?
faq.answer: Yes. It writes graph block content for the Obsidian Desmos plugin syntax.

faq.question: Can it render the graph for me?
faq.answer: No. It prepares the block text, but rendering happens in Obsidian with the plugin installed.

faq.question: Why does pi syntax change between sections?
faq.answer: Settings use mathjs syntax, while equations and points use Desmos LaTeX syntax.

faq.question: Can it help with parser errors?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains common errors and rewrites graph syntax to avoid them.

faq.question: Does it support styling?
faq.answer: Yes. It can apply supported colors, line styles, point styles, labels, and hidden helper functions.

faq.question: Is it useful for advanced curves?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers parametric curves, polar equations, piecewise functions, and conversion guidance.
